text: A penalty is charged when rent is paid after the due date.
Interest accrues on any overdue amount owed to the landlord.
A fixed fee applies if a payment instrument is returned unpaid.
The penalty for delay compounds for each period the arrears continue.
The deposit is returned only after a long delay following handover.
The landlord decides unilaterally what to deduct from the deposit.
The deposit is forfeited if the tenant leaves before the agreed date.
The deposit is large relative to the monthly rent and earns no interest.
The tenant pays for repairs that would normally fall to the owner.
Structural upkeep of the building is shifted onto the occupant.
Repair costs below a threshold are always the tenant's responsibility.
The tenant may not deduct money spent on repairs from the rent.
Leaving before the minimum period still requires paying the balance.
An extended notice period applies before the tenant may move out.
A fixed number of months rent is payable as damages for early exit.
Money owed on departure is taken out of the deposit.
The rent rises by a set percentage at fixed intervals.
The owner may raise the rent during the term at short notice.
Staying on after a notice counts as agreeing to the new rent.
An increase takes effect without any fresh agreement being signed.
The owner may come into the property without telling the occupant first.
Inspections may happen at any time the owner considers reasonable.
The property may be shown to other people while still occupied.
The occupant may not refuse access when it is demanded.
The occupant may not let anyone else use any part of the property.
Breaking the occupancy restriction ends the agreement immediately.
Only the people named in the document may live in the property.
Adding another occupant triggers a higher payment.
The agreement renews by itself unless notice is given well in advance.
Automatic continuation comes with a higher payment than before.
A notice counts as delivered even if it never reached the recipient.
A long notice window must be observed to avoid being bound again.
Taxes and levies on the property are passed to the occupant.
Association or society dues are payable by the occupant.
Any future charge imposed by an authority becomes the occupant's burden.
An increase in recurring charges is absorbed entirely by the occupant.
The property must be handed back in its original state at the occupant's cost.
Anything the occupant installed must be removed before leaving.
Repainting is payable regardless of the actual condition on exit.
The cost of putting the property right falls on the departing occupant.
